title: Chelsea's Brady stake talks are a sideshow they can do without
body:
Chelsea are the latest club to have a famous name circling their boardroom, with Tom Brady reported to be in talks about buying a small stake [S1].

The background is specific. Brady has reportedly parted with a minority holding in Birmingham City, which he had owned for three years, and sources told the Guardian the move was meant to clear the way for investment at Stamford Bridge [S1]. He is said to have a strong relationship with Behdad Eghbali [S1]. He was also a Chelsea guest at last year's Club World Cup in New Jersey, where he was seen celebrating with the players after their 3-0 final win over Paris Saint-Germain [S1].

The on-pitch picture is more mixed. In the last five league matches, Chelsea have won three, drawn none and lost two, taking nine points from a sequence of win, win, loss, win, loss [ST1]. They have scored nine and conceded four in that run [ST1]. That is a side with real attacking punch and a back line that is holding up well enough, which makes a distraction harder to justify.

A famous investor brings noise faster than goals. That is not a crisis, but it is not a platform for grand promises either. The smart money is on patience: rushed deals rarely age well, and talk is cheap until the paperwork is signed.

The Touchline Take: judge the business when the window shuts, not before.

evidence.text: The Guardian: Tom Brady in talks over buying Chelsea stake after Birmingham City exit. NFL legend was Chelsea guest at Club World Cup. Brady has good relationship with Behdad Eghbali. Tom Brady is in discussions about buying a small stake in Chelsea. The NFL legend sold a minority share in Birmingham City after three years this month, a move sources have told the Guardian was to pave the way for investing at Stamford Bridge. Brady was a guest of Chelsea when Enzo Maresca’s then side won the Club World Cup in New Jersey last year and was seen celebrating with the players after their remarkable 3-0 final win over Paris Saint-Germain.
